definition_sources.name: LuxAlgo library: Bullish/bearish Order Block
what_it_says: An order block is the last candle that closed against a move before the move took off; a run of consecutive opposite candles can be boxed as a single zone.

The candle alone is not the concept: the move away has to show displacement, speed and range that break structure or trade through a prior swing, ideally leaving a fair value gap. A liquidity sweep before the move is a grading factor, not a requirement.
Drawing conventions vary and none is official: the candle's full high-to-low range (most common), the body only, the open to the extreme, or a refinement to the 50% mean threshold.
Entry on the return is commonly combined with a lower-timeframe change of character inside the zone; a decisive close through the entire zone invalidates the block.
No reliable universal hit rate exists; order blocks fail routinely.
not_specified: how many candles make the move
how far the move must travel
which swing must be broken and how a swing is defined

definition_sources.name: TMGM academy: Order Block in Trading
what_it_says: An order block is the last opposite candle before an impulsive move; the impulsive move is described as much bigger than the candles around it, with no size given.
Marked from the candle high to the candle low, wicks included; a valid block usually comes before a break of structure and often leaves a fair value gap.
Traders enter only after the retest and a sign of confirmation; the worked example enters after a rejection candle inside the block.
Usually treated as invalid once a candle closes beyond its far edge, though tools and teachers differ.
Order blocks do not predict price and many fail; marking one is subjective and easier in hindsight.
FAQ: the concept was named and popularised by Michael J. Huddleston (Inner Circle Trader), mainly through his free online videos; the basic idea is older than ICT.
not_specified: how long a block stays valid

definition_sources.name: TradingView: Smart Money Concepts (SMC) [LuxAlgo], open-source script
what_it_says: Order blocks highlight areas where institutional market participants open positions.
When price breaks through an order block the indicator considers it mitigated and removes it.
States there is no supporting data regarding the validity of these teachings.

what_it_says: Introduces Michael J. Huddleston as The Inner Circle Trader and links to his YouTube lectures.
does_not_say: The term 'order block' does not appear on the home page; no dates for when any term was introduced.
origin.conclusion: No dated, written primary source for the term was found. The article attributes the naming claim to TMGM's page and attributes no wording to Huddleston.
